title: Elucidating the FOXF1 gene regulatory network in human alveologenesis
text:
(PROJECT NARRATIVE)
Mutations in the FOXF1 gene locus are associated with alveolar-capillary dysplasia with misalignment of
pulmonary veins, a lethal lung developmental disorder with no cure. This project aims to uncover the molecular
mechanism underlying FOXF1-mediated abnormalities in alveolar endothelial cell subtypes, and the disrupted
endothelial-epithelial interactions during lung development. If successful, the proposed studies will uncover the
FOXF gene regulatory network in human lung, and provide new therapeutic targets to re-establish normal
alveolar-capillary interface in various lung developmental disorders.

title: The path to the parous brain: allopregnanolone-mediated mechanisms at GABAA receptors.
text:
Pregnancy is characterized by marked changes in circulating hormones that can induce long-lasting changes in
the brain. The goal of this project is to determine how the hormone allopregnanolone may induce a robust neural
inhibition in the medial prefrontal cortex during pregnancy, resulting in over-compensatory actions that persist
well after birth. Our work will provide much-needed insight into the development of the brain post-pregnancy.

title: High accuracy automated tick classification using computer vision
text:
Project Narrative. Current tick identification methods are highly resource and labor intensive, requiring
physical collection of specimens and subsequent identification of species, sex, life stage, and
engorgement by an acarologist based on visual morphological inspection. Here we propose to advance a
prototype deep learning system capable of instantaneously and accurately identifying twelve
medically-relevant adult tick species with 98% accuracy for practical deployment in professional public
health and the general public. The resulting products developed through this proposal will ultimately
expand tick surveillance capability and capacity, and strengthen public health response to tick-borne
diseases.

title: Enabling Focused Ultrasound-Activated Gene Editing with Thermo-Controlled CRISPR-Cas9
text:
CRISPR-based medicines have the potential to address many genetic diseases, which remain
otherwise incurable, by editing the human genome. However, two of the greatest barriers to broad clinical
application of CRISPR therapeutics are delivery to specific tissues and organs in the human body and the
potential for editing in the wrong places, known as off-target editing. To potentially address these
significant challenges, we propose to build and test CRISPR enzymes that can respond to a narrow
temperature range safe for the body that can eventually be combined with focused ultrasound, enabling
future therapeutic gene editing technologies that can be activated and controlled non-invasively.

title: Image-guided robotic assistance to improve precision and reduce x-ray dose in orthopedic surgery for pediatric SCFE
text:
Placement of orthopaedic implants, such as a K-wires and screws, is a common surgical task,
and accurate placement is critical to the success of a wide range of orthopaedic procedures.
However, the rate of screw misplacement is highly variable which can lead to poor outcomes. In
this proposal we will develop and evaluate a system that should improve the surgeon’s ability to
accurately place the screw while minimizing radiation dose to the patient and surgeon.

title: Targeting Undruggable SMAD4 HyperPPI with Myhre iPSC Biosensors and Organoids
text:
NARATIVE
Myhre Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that causes severe fibrosis, heart disease, and vascular problems,
for which there are currently no effective treatments. This project will use patient-derived stem cells and 3D
cardiac organoids to model how a mutation in the driver SMAD4 gene disrupts key protein interactions and drives
disease. By developing new tools to study and eventually target these “undruggable” protein interactions, this
work will lay the foundation for therapies to improve the health of individuals with Myhre Syndrome and related
conditions.

title: Molecular Mechanisms Underlying Endothelial Weibel-Palade Body Biogenesis and Exocytosis
text:
von Willebrand factor (vWF) is essential for normal hemostasis and thrombosis and is involved in other
important processes such as angiogenesis and cancer cell metastasis. Regulated release of vWF depends on
normal maturation of its storage granule, the Weibel-Palade bodies (WPBs), and subsequent fusion of WPBs
to the plasma membrane, processes which are poorly understood. Using live cell microscopy, pulldown of
endogenously tagged proteins, and a genetically modified mouse model, we propose to elucidate the
endosomal pathway in WPB biogenesis, the associated trafficking machinery, and regulation of WPB
exocytosis by the exocyst complex.

title: iPSC Processing Core
text: (CORE B - iPSC Biobank Core): The Core B serves as a critical pillar in the collective efforts of this Program Project. Its central mission is to support and empower all projects and cores by providing essential resources, infrastructure, and expertise focused on induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and their pivotal role in unraveling the intricacies of cardiotoxicity associated with cancer therapeutics.

title: Designing a targeted 'super adjuvant' nanoparticle platform for vaccination
text:
In complex diseases like cancer, a single-adjuvant vaccine may not be fully effective to mitigate the myriad
immunosuppressive effects of a heterogeneous aggressive tumor microenvironment such as that of triple-
negative breast cancer. Co-delivery of multiple adjuvants in a rationally designed “super adjuvant” formulation
can harness multiple pattern recognition receptor pathways simultaneously to drive a proinflammatory
synergistic cytokine response that has both breadth and depth. Here we propose to design a tumor-targeted
“super adjuvant” immunomodulatory nanoparticle platform for in situ cancer vaccination that coencapsulates 3
synergistic innate agonists of the STING, TLR4, and TLR9 pathways to promote Type I interferon-mediated
anti-tumor immunity.

title: Developing a cCRE-Centric Infrastructure in AnVIL to Characterize Variant Effects on Gene Regulation
text:
Understanding how genetic variation influences gene regulation is essential for uncovering the biological
mechanisms underlying human health and disease. This project will develop scalable computational tools to
study how noncoding genetic variants impact transcriptional regulation at the single-cell and isoform levels,
advancing our ability to interpret genetic disease risk factors. By integrating large-scale genomic data into the
AnVIL cloud platform, this work will create widely accessible resources that enhance genetic research and
contribute to the understanding of regulatory mechanisms driving human diseases.

title: Multi-omics Strategies to Improve Clinical Outcomes in Uveitis
text:
Uveitis is a significant cause of blindness globally and there are many challenges to diagnose infectious
etiologies due to the insensitivity of diagnostic testing and limited sample volumes from the intraocular space.
This proposal leverages international collaborators and recent technological advancements in deep
sequencing and mass spectrometry to identify pathogens causing uveitis and characterize the host
transcriptome in intraocular fluid and interrogate the tears for proteome and metabolite profiles. This study will
provide a comprehensive molecular approach to improve the diagnosis of uveitis and deepen our
understanding of the host response to improve the characterization of infectious uveitis syndromes through
pathogen discovery and contribute to future risk stratification, individualized treatment, and biomarker
identification in uveitis.

title: Targeting base damage repair in BRCA-mutant cancers
text:
Mutations in DNA repair genes called BRCA1 and 2 increase pre-disposition to multiple cancers. Currently
BRCA mutant cancer cells are treated with inhibitors of Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) enzymes;
however, this treatment strategy has multiple limitations. In this proposal, we will develop a framework to
overcome the clinical limitations of PARP inhibitors and hence provide an effective strategy for the treatment
of BRCA mutant cancers.

title: Dynamic Cognitive Phenotypes for Prediction of Mental Health Outcomes in Serious Mental Illness
text:
The proposed project will develop and validate methods to quantify fluctuations in cognitive information
processing for clinical prediction models to (1) identify at-risk individuals, and (2) identify risk periods, enabling
timely interventions to improve time to recovery, prevent symptom escalation, and reduce hospitalizations.
Further, we will validate our assessment tools and prediction models in ethnoracially diverse communities to
ensure generalizability and improve mental health equity.

title: Single-cell Joint Profiling of Single- and Double-Stranded DNA Breaks with Transcriptome
text:
Defects in DNA repair pathways promote cancer progression but also presents a therapeutic opportunity.
However, analyzing DNA damage and its influence on gene programs in heterogeneous cancer samples
remained challenging. To fill this technical gap, we will develop a multimodal single-cell technique to sequence
single-strand-, double-strand- DNA breaks with transcriptome.

title: Functional and Radiomic Magnetic Resonance Profiling in Normal and Hypertensive Placentas
text:
Pregnant women with chronic hypertension are at an increased risk for placental-mediated disease, as 1 in 3
pregnant women with chronic hypertension deliver preterm from complications of superimposed preeclampsia
or fetal growth restriction. This project will address the unmet clinical need to characterize placental
dysfunction throughout pregnancy, focusing specifically on differences in functional magnetic resonance
imaging metrics of perfusion, diffusion, and oxygenation and radiomics texture features between normal
pregnant women and pregnant women with chronic hypertension. Furthermore, execution of automated
segmentation through deep learning will be performed to standardize and improve the efficiency of post-
processing.

title: Shared Journeys of Firearm Violence Survivors and Their Caregivers
text:
Firearm violence is a public health crisis in the U.S., with survivors facing lasting physical and mental health
challenges. Many survivors do not engage with formal support services (e.g., violence intervention programs,
mental health counseling) due to distrust and stigma as well as a preference for receiving support from informal
caregivers, often family or friends. The proposed training project will examine the recovery experiences of
survivors and their caregivers to identify barriers, facilitators, and relationship dynamics, potentially informing
future interventions that improve engagement and support for both groups.

title: Virtual Twin-Powered Rapid Development of Bioactive Multifunctional Dental Restoratives
text:
This project aims to develop a streamlined platform for the fast development of an innovative
system of bioactive dental restoratives that is characterized by its self-healing and dynamic capabilities that
may be tailored to individual patient needs. Employing hybrid modeling and simulation approaches, we will
refine the formulation and guide the precise placement of restorative materials for effective caries treatment.

title: Identifying Recovery Insights through Signal Extraction (iRISE): Leveraging Machine Learning Strategies to Predict Disengagement from Recovery Communities
text:
This project is relevant to public health because recovery communities for addiction support and long-term
recovery from substance use have migrated toward digital spaces. While multiple frameworks exist to predict
recovery maintenance within in-person recovery communities, we lack digital analogs that can effectively identify
waning recovery to promote timely encouragement and additional support if needed. Using data science to track
the language, emotions, and behaviors extracted from a recovery community mobile app, we can produce a
scalable tool as an analog of recovery maintenance; this tool is a first step in a comprehensive plan to develop
solutions to digital recovery maintenance.

title: Role of tRNA- and rRNA-derived RNAs in acute lung injury
text:
Acute lung injury (ALI) is a clinical syndrome of acute respiratory failure with high morbidity and mortality, and is
associated with an uncontrolled inflammatory response due to excessive production of cytokines and other
inflammatory mediators. We recently discovered a significant upregulation of specific tRNA- and rRNA-derived
short non-coding RNAs (sncRNAs) in a Lipopolysaccharide-induced ALI model. Our project aims to
comprehensively investigate the dysregulation of these sncRNAs in human and mouse ALI models and to
elucidate their role in cytokine overproduction and immune cell infiltration, thus contributing to a deeper
understanding of the molecular pathogenesis of ALI.

title: Investigating the mechanisms of driver genes associated with ancestry and aggressiveness in prostate cancer
text:
We will perform whole exome sequencing (WES) of prostate cancers from AA men to find additional molecular
alterations associated with aggressiveness in African American (AA) men. We will also apply single-cell RNA-
seq and mass spectrometry to prostate organoid cultures to characterize differences in the cellular states
between ancestral backgrounds. Finally, we will validate the functional effects of ancestry- and grade-associated
driver alterations in different ancestral backgrounds using novel prostate cell lines derived directly from patients.
